message.content: {"caption":"Diagram of an agent inspecting a conversation transcript, building and refining a memory, and answering a question using that memory.","description":"A process diagram has four main stages. At upper left, a blue panel contains “Memory Principles”: keep memory useful, accurate, cheap, and safe for future conversation, with bullets “Source-backed,” “Latest-aware,” “Auditable,” “Flexible format,” and “…”; a small shield/check icon sits beside the list. Below it, “Memory Action Space” lists “Read the transcript,” “Read current memory,” “Write or revise memory,” “Check memory quality,” “Self-test / improve memory process,” and “Extend the memory toolkit.” Small document/gear and target/check motifs accompany the toolkit item. A gray arrow points right from this panel toward a blue robot labeled “Agent.” Above the robot, a yellow “Transcript store” box says “272 turns,” “136 user / 136 assistant,” and “Stored as SQLite:” followed by turns( turn_index, turn_id, role, time_anchor, content, rendered, char_count ). An unlabeled gray arrow points down from the store to the upper agent. Another gray arrow points right from that agent into the large orange “Memory Trajectory” panel. The panel shows ten numbered actions: 1. “Inspect transcript” using “conversation_manifest()”: 272 turns; 136 user + 136 assistant. 2. “Skim beginning” using “SQL ASC LIMIT 5”: Darryl asks about comfy sneakers. 3. “Skim ending” using “SQL DESC LIMIT 5”: Aug 20 / Aug 22 event topics. 4. “Count roles” using “SQL GROUP BY role”: confirms paired chat structure. 5. “Search candidate facts” using “SQL LIKE keywords”: sneaker, budget, festival, location rows. 6. “Inspect memory” using “memory_read(“workspace”)”: checks current memory state. 7. “Write broad profile” using “memory_change(...)”: Darryl + preferences + entities + dates. 8. “Review quality” using “memory_review(...)”: warns stale facts / broad memory. 9. “Refine memory” using “memory_change(...)”: stable preferences only. 10. “Audit source turns” using “SQL turn_index IN (...)”: verifies source rows. A small yellow looping-arrow-like icon sits by “Memory Trajectory.” An unlabeled downward arrow leads from this panel to a blue box titled “SelfMem Memory Generated by Agent.” Its bullets read: “User: Darryl”; “Stable sneaker preferences: comfort, neutral colors, arch support, breathable materials, grip”; “Stable people: Kyle, Lauren, Maureen, Fred, Bradley, Christopher”; “Stable locations: East Janethaven, Foot Locker, Montserrat, SneakerLab, Finish Line”; and “…” . An unlabeled gray arrow points left from this memory box to a second blue robot labeled “Agent.” To the robot’s left are two speech bubbles: a pink question, “How many days passed between when I got the size 11 Ultraboot and when I reordered the size 11.5?” and a green reply, “One day passed between when I got the size 11 Ultraboot on April 30 and when I reordered the size 11.5 on May 1.” The reply bubble has a green check badge. No chart data are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
